metadata.case_name: PETER THURSTON PIPER AND ANOTHER v. NANCY FRANCIS TANG

injuries.description: ligamentous strain and aggravation of pre-existing disc narrowing.
source: Dr. Da Roza, who diagnosed ligamentous strain and aggravation of pre-existing disc narrowing.

injuries.description: posterior fusion of vertebrae L4-5 and L5-S1, bilateral screw fixation of the posterior joints and an onlay bone graft taken from the left sacro-iliac crest.
source: an operation was carried out on the plaintiff's spine consisting of posterior fusion of vertebrae L4-5 and L5-S1, bilateral screw fixation of the posterior joints and an onlay bone graft taken from the left sacro-iliac crest.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: pain in her back and left hip, the donor area
source: She still had considerable pain in her back and left hip, the donor area, and could not sleep on her left side, which is her normal side for sleeping, for several weeks.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of pelvis

manifestations.description: severe pains in her lower back
intense pain requiring painkillers and time off work
difficulty getting out of bed and loosened up in the morning which used to take about ½ hour and included the use of the wall for support
considerable pain in her back and left hip post-operatively
trouble sleeping on occasions; could not sleep on her left side for several weeks
stiffness in backwards bending of the spine; restriction is likely to be permanent
unable to go out for long periods without undue pain in her back occurring

treatments_received: posterior fusion of vertebrae L4-5 and L5-S1
bilateral screw fixation of the posterior joints
onlay bone graft taken from the left sacro-iliac crest
corset with addition of metal rods in the back

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: She employed a full-time amah as she could do none of the housework. This situation still obtains.
Because of her condition, the plaintiff cannot go out for long periods without undue pain in her back occurring. Thus, she is unable to take her children out as much as before the accident.
Her social life is curtailed; she used to drive the family around; now she drives as little as possible and uses public transport.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: She took part in squash, badminton, drama and keep fit; it will either be impossible or difficult to return to these activities. She used to enjoy dancing but can now only do so in a very limited fashion.
Stiffness in backwards bending of the spine which is only to be expected after such an operation. This restriction is likely to be permanent.

comparable_cases.injury_description: whiplash injuries to her neck; between February 1967 and June 1968 she wore a neck collar

comparable_cases.case_name: Liu Ying-muk v. Choi Lun-kui & Anr.
comparable_cases.injury_description: Damage to the plaintiff's spine left him paralysed from the waist down. The plaintiff was 50; he was not expected to live beyond 60.
